summary: Most damage comes from splitting inside tightly bound grammatical units — conditionals, converbs, and rhetorical-question scopes — or from over-splitting disfluent filler-heavy speech. Meanwhile many long, cleanly-structured sentences (with sentence-initial connectives, embedded questions, or quotative clauses) were left completely unsegmented, and reference-segmentation evidence shows free latency gains were missed there. The prompt should split more often at low-risk boundaries (after fillers/connectives, after quoted/embedded questions) and less often inside conditional or converb-linked clauses.
